_readme: Suppressions for scripts/scan-secrets.py. Key: "<path>:<label>:<digest>", value: the reason.
The digest is the truncated SHA-256 the scanner prints; the value itself never appears here.
An entry with an empty reason makes the scanner refuse to run at all, so waiving the gate is
a visible, reviewable act rather than a silent one.
This file starts EMPTY on purpose. It was NOT copied from another repository in this estate:
an allowlist inherited from a different tree accepts findings nobody here ever looked at, and
the first thing it would hide is the thing this repository most needs to see.
Nothing live is ever allowlisted. A committed credential is compromised from the commit, not
from the discovery — the remedy is rotation at the provider and then removal. Recording its
digest here would turn the one gate that noticed into the reason nobody notices again.
